content:
maira: heads up — after the 4f3c9b2 merge we see token/sec dip on ctb workers in eu-west-1, started ~09:12 UTC. p95 latency up too.
jonas: saw that on dashboards, spike in queueing delays and long tail. any obvious correlates?
sandeep: I profiled a host and noticed a lot more kernel handoffs during drain, coalesce wait times increased. attaching quick snapshot.
maira: can you paste the profiler snippet?
sandeep: ```
flame: continuous-batcher::coalesce_wait  1.8s (↑210%)
flame: scheduler::handoff           0.9s (↑160%)
metrics: tokens/sec                820 (baseline ~1120)
kv_cache/hit_rate                 0.72 -> 0.61
```
lucy: wow kv hit rate drop too. do we think smoothing change affected batching boundaries and so KV reuse?
jonas: PR 4128 changed burst_smoothing heuristic to prefer tighter windows for low-latency, looks like it prevents coalescing of adjacent small requests so we get more tiny batches -> kernel swap churn.
maira: CI perf job flagged this on the canary build, but it was marginal and got dismissed in the rush to release. perf-ci, can you paste the CI comparison?
perf-ci: automated result: `compare/perf-4128` -> throughput -26.8% on ctb-eu-west baseline B, p95 latency +34%. Baseline runs: 2026-03-17T08:00:00Z.
maira: that's enough to block rollout. can someone bisect the change?
sandeep: running git bisect now across commits touching scheduler/batching. taking hosts from the failing pool.
jonas: quick note, reverting just the smoothing tweak locally restores throughput to ~98% of baseline and KV hit returns to ~0.7.
sandeep: bisect narrowed it down to commit 4f3c9b2 -> the kernel affinity hint added in that commit. the heuristic interplay is the culprit; ordering of apply() causes windows to shrink before coalesce step.
maira: plan: 1) hold rollout 2) revert 4f3c9b2 on canary 3) open hotfix PR that reorders smoothing vs coalesce, add regression test 4) run full perf CI.
lucy: I'll queue the rollback and tag infra to pin canary to previous image.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated: canary -> image redwood/runtime:2026-03-16-b3f. Reason: perf degradation detected.
perf-ci: running full suite; preliminary shows tokens/sec restored to 1090, p95 back within 5% of baseline. final results expected in ~30m.
jonas: adding a unit + integration test: simulate micro-bursts and assert coalesce window not below min_threshold. also adding a KV-hit regression check.
maira: thanks. assign follow-ups: @sandeep to PR hotfix + bench, @jonas to tests, @lucy to coordinate rollout once CI green.
sandeep: one more datapoint — this only manifested on ctb mode (continuous coalescing) where small inter-arrival variance is high. non-ctb endpoints unaffected. raises question about gate/flag defaults.
maira: agree, we should default conservative smoothing until we have perf signal. open item for product to decide.
jonas: I'll draft the PR now. expect draft in 45m.
maira: great. please post perf CI link here when green. :thumbsup:
